senses.gloss: to join, put together, put up, erect, restore (to proper position).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 2:6">Bets. II, 6</cite> <he>אין זוֹקְפִין וכ׳</he> you must not set up (put together the links of) a lamp on a Holy Day (v.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 27a:4">M. Kat. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>מאימתי זוֹקְפִין וכ׳</he> from what time on the eve of the Sabbath are the mourners’ couches put up again? <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 46a:16">Ab. Zar. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>ז׳ לבינה וכ׳</he> if one put a brick up to worship it, v. <cite ref="G00636"><he>זְקִיפָה</he></cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="G00627"><he>זָקוּף</he></cite>, f. <cite ref="G00629"><he>זְקוּפָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 3:7">M. Kat. III, 7</cite> <he>מטה ז׳</he> a put-up couch, opp. <he>מ׳ כפויה</he> an upset couch whereon mourners are seated; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (cmp. לָוָה a. Lat. nexus) to establish a loan, to obligate, enjoin upon (with על).
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 72a:4">B. Mets. 72ᵃ</cite> <he>וזְקָפָן עליו במלוה</he> and the creditor settles the interests on the debtor as a loan (the note stating the combined amount of principle and interest as principle).
<cite ref="Gittin 18a:11">Gitt. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>עד שתפגום ותִזְקוֹף</he> until she accepts partial payment (of her widowhood) and settles the balance as a loan (by taking a note &c.).
<cite ref="Gittin 18a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>זָקְפָה ולא פגמה</he> if she allows her widowhood to be entered as a loan without taking a partial payment.
<cite ref="Gittin 18a:12">Ib.</cite> <he>אונס … שזְקָפָן במלוה</he> indemnity for outrage, fines … which were settled in the way of a loan; a. e.

senses.gloss: (neut. verb) to stand upright, to be restored again.
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 59b:3">B. Mets. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>לא נפלו … ולא זָקְפוּ</he> the bent walls did not fall, nor did they assume their straight position.
<cite ref="Berakhot 11a:15">Ber. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>וז׳ ר׳ ישמ׳</he> R. Y. remained upright, opp. <cite ref="N00555"><he>הִטָּה</he></cite>.

Ib. כשאני … אתה זָקַפְתָּ when I bowed, thou didst remain upright. Y. ib. IV, beg. 7ᵃ זוֹקֵף he erects himself (from his bowed position).—Part. pass. זָקוּף, f. זְקוּפָה upright, erect. Ber. l. c.—קומה זקופה erect stature, proud carriage. Ib. 43ᵇ; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be put up, to erect one’s self. Tosef. ib. I, 6; Sifré Deut. 34; a. e.
to be converted into a loan. Gitt. l. c. מאימתי נִזְקָפִים במלוה from what time are fines &c. considered as converted loans (so as to be subject to limitation)?
